questions.question: Why do production audio generators use neural codecs before a transformer models the sound?
options: They compress long waveforms into discrete token sequences
They remove the need for a decoder or vocoder
They make every audio sample independent of its neighbors
They convert the waveform directly into natural-language captions
questions.explanation: Neural codecs compress a long waveform into lower-rate discrete codebook tokens, giving an autoregressive model a tractable sequence to predict. A codec still needs decoding to turn generated tokens back into sound.

questions.question: At 75 frames per second with 8 RVQ codebooks, how many codec tokens are emitted each second?
options: 8 tokens per second
75 tokens per second
6,000 tokens per second
600 tokens per second
questions.explanation: Each of 75 codec frames contributes an index from each of 8 RVQ codebooks, so 75 frames/s × 8 indices/frame = 600 tokens/s. A rate of 6,000 would require ten times as many indices per second.

questions.question: Which audio-generation approach is naturally suited to live streaming?
options: A classifier that predicts the next speaker label
Token-autoregressive generation over codec codes
Latent diffusion over a fixed-length clip
A one-shot GAN over raw audio samples
questions.explanation: Token-autoregressive generation emits codec codes causally, one step after its available context, which supports streaming playback. The described latent flow-matching systems generate a fixed clip and need chunking and overlap to stream.

questions.question: What does MusicGen’s delayed-parallel strategy do with RVQ codebook streams?
options: Combines all codebooks into one continuous waveform first
Uses one codebook and discards the remaining residuals
Predicts each audio sample independently at 24 kHz
Emits the streams in parallel with staggered offsets
questions.explanation: MusicGen’s delayed-parallel method emits multiple RVQ codebook streams with staggered time offsets, rather than serially flattening all streams. That reduces the effective sequence length while preserving their temporal alignment.

questions.question: A live voice-chat product needs audio to arrive as it is produced. Which model family should the team prioritize?
options: Fixed-clip flow matching
Offline VAE reconstruction
Image-conditioned diffusion only
Codec autoregressive generation
questions.explanation: For live voice chat, codec AR can produce tokens incrementally at the playback rate; the production note recommends it for real-time streaming. Flow matching renders a fixed clip and is better suited to on-submit generation.

questions.question: A generator produces artifacts because its codec cannot represent a particular sound faithfully. What is the likely ceiling?
options: Higher sampling temperature will restore the missing detail
A longer text prompt will add unsupported waveform detail
Generator quality cannot exceed the codec’s representation
More transformer layers will change the codec’s codebook
questions.explanation: Output fidelity is bounded by what the codec representation can encode: discarded acoustic detail is unavailable to the later generator. More transformer layers cannot change the codec codebook or recover information removed before modeling.
